news_drafts.headline: Flintshire: none of its £18.95m of LOBO bank loans was called in the six months to September 2026
news_drafts.lead:
None of Flintshire Council's £18.95m of LOBO loans was called in the six months to September 2026, according to papers for its Governance and Audit Committee meeting on 24 November. A LOBO is a bank loan where, on set dates, the lender may propose a higher interest rate and the council may then repay the loan in full instead of accepting it. The council held the £18.95m on 1 April 2026, and all of it had semi-annual call dates in that period.

The papers say the loans also have call dates within the next 12 months, and that the council has liaised with the firm Arlingclose on the likelihood of the options being exercised. If a lender proposed a revised rate, the council says it "plans to repay the loan at no additional cost as accepting the revised terms would mean the Council would still have refinancing risk in later years." Replacement funding would come from cash, other local authorities or the Public Works Loan Board, the government's lending arm for councils. The paper gives no figure for the cost of replacement funding.

A schedule of loans at 30 September 2026 lists the LOBO block at £18.95m, with annual interest of £858,095. The three loans carry rates of 4.48%, 4.53% and 4.58%, and mature between January 2040 and January 2042.

news_drafts.headline: Flintshire projects a £7.625m gross overspend at Month 6, down from £8.493m at Month 5
news_drafts.lead:
Flintshire Council is projecting a gross operating deficit of £7.625m on the Council Fund for 2026/27 at Month 6, according to a report to its Corporate Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee. Using the whole of the remaining £2.704m budget risk reserve would reduce that to a net deficit of £4.921m. The gross figure is £0.868m lower than the £8.493m reported at Month 5, with £1.800m released from deferred ultra-low emission vehicle infrastructure costs and a £0.507m grant set against fleet borrowing costs among the movements.

Out of County Placements are projected at £28.345m against a £25.706m budget, an overspend of £2.639m, even though £2m was added to the budget. The paper says further net placements are "highly likely". The rest of Social Services is projected at £122.275m against £117.240m, an overspend of £5.035m. Children's professional support teams are £0.625m overspent, largely from agency costs because of "challenges recruiting and retaining social workers". The council projects that 82% of its £10.999m of budget reductions will be achieved, leaving a £2.015m shortfall.

Unearmarked reserves are projected at £9.751m after the overspend, down from £18.261m at the start of the year. School reserves stood at a deficit of £4.798m at 31 March 2026, an adverse movement of £4.199m. The paper says school deficits are projected to exceed £8m by 31 March 2027. The 3.5% teachers' pay award from September 2026 compares with the 3.2% in the settlement and the 3.0% the council budgeted. Welsh Government grant covers part of the gap, and the paper says a residual shortfall "will need to be met from within existing resources".

news_drafts.headline: Flintshire's contingency reserve falls from £8.272m to £0.748m after one-off costs and a Month 5 forecast
news_drafts.lead:
Flintshire Council's contingency reserve, the money held back for the unexpected, is down to £0.748m from £8.272m, according to a paper before its Cabinet on 13 October 2026. The reserve is the part of its reserves, the money it has put aside, that sits above the base level the council keeps.

The largest call on it is a projected outturn of £5.789m at Month 5. Outturn is the actual spending figure for a year once it has ended, as against what was budgeted. Here it is a projection part-way through the year. The paper also sets out three one-off pressures the reserve is to fund: £0.142m for children's services legal costs, £0.165m to put in place SharePoint, a document-sharing software system, and £0.036m for temporary posts.

The four items named in the paper do not by themselves account for the whole fall from £8.272m to £0.748m. The material does not itemise the remainder. The paper's total line reads "Total Contingency Reserve 0.748".

findings.headline: Flintshire Bridge 10-year special inspection due in 2028/29, with £1.3m anticipated for capital works and actual costs unknown until inspections complete
findings.detail: The paper says special inspections must be carried out every 10 years and are capitalised. The cost of any works depends on the inspection results, and the Council is still seeking Welsh Government or trunk road agency agreement to transfer the A548 section.
findings.matters: A large fixed-interval inspection on a single asset with an unknown capital outcome is the kind of exposure a finance officer at another council with similar infrastructure will want to plan for.
findings.figures: £1.3m anticipated capital works; 10-year inspection cycle; due in 2028/29
findings.quote: for which we anticipate £1.3m will be required. However, actual costs are unknown until these inspections are completed.

findings.headline: County Hall demolition phase three costs £4.9m from the Council's capital budget, with £4.500m in 2027/28 under the Office Rationalisation Programme
findings.detail: The paper says the programme will cut rates, utilities and security costs, and reduce the estate's carbon footprint. It also says demolition phases one and two of the remaining County Hall building are funded in 2027/28, with £0.400m already in the previous programme.
findings.matters: A demolition programme that the Council expects to reduce revenue costs is a commitment a finance officer elsewhere may compare against estate rationalisation plans.
findings.quote: Capital investment of £4.9m utilised from the Council’s capital programme budget.

findings.headline: ALN specialist provision: the Council's study estimates £45 million needed for a long-term solution, with a 75% Welsh Government contribution rate for specialist provision
findings.detail: The paper says the immediate Ysgol Croes Atti refurbishment costs £5m, of which £1.5m is grant and £3.5m is borrowing. The paper says the wider investment is a Strategic Outline Programme item.
findings.matters: Growing demand for specialist school places, with waiting lists introduced for the first time, is a pressure on councils with out-of-county placement costs.
findings.figures: £45 million long-term investment estimate; £5m capital investment for Ysgol Croes Atti; £1.5m ALN grant; £3.5m borrowing; £13.7m revenue cost of borrowing over 50 years; 75% WG rate
findings.quote: Its findings indicate that an investment of approximately £45 million would be required to deliver a sustainable, long-term solution

findings.headline: Highways Asset Management Plan core allocation of £2m a year, against £5.2m estimated to maintain current network performance
findings.detail: The paper says the Local Government Borrowing Initiative grant funded £5.665m across 2025/26 and 2026/27. Funding beyond 2026/27 has not been confirmed, and the paper describes the resulting gap as significant.
findings.matters: A council whose one-off grant for road maintenance is ending, with the gap to maintain performance stated, is a pressure any highways authority will recognise.
findings.figures: £2m per year core allocation; £5.2m per year to maintain current performance; £3.2m per year increase; £5.665m LGBI grant across 2025/26 and 2026/27
findings.quote: The core Capital Programme includes £2m per annum for the HAMP. It has been estimated that the investment required to maintain current network performance is £5.2m per annum, an increase of £3.2m per annum.

findings.headline: Joint Archive Facility costs rise by £1.596m at RIBA Stage 3, with Council core funding £0.862m, or £0.427m if grant secured
findings.detail: The paper says the increase came from design development and a cost review. The Council will fund £0.862m from core funding if grant does not materialise, and could reduce this to about £0.427m if further grant is secured.
findings.matters: A cost increase at detailed design stage, with the Council's contribution set as a worst case, is the kind of overrun a finance officer at another council will check against their own archive or civic projects.
findings.figures: £1.596m increase in overall project costs; £0.862m additional core funding; about £0.427m if grant is secured; £12.667m estimated funding available; £2.882m borrowing over 50 years
findings.quote: has identified an increase in overall project costs of approximately £1.596m.

daily_post.headline: One of the fund's property managers, Darwin, has had "significant decline in valuation" after specific performance and strategy issues.
daily_post.lead: A manager-level valuation decline within a property allocation is a risk that a finance officer at any fund holding the same manager would need to assess.
